title: CASE OF BEKOS AND KOUTROPOULOS v. GREECE
conclusion: Violations of Art. 3;No separate issue under Art. 13;No violation of Art. 14+3 (alleged racist treatment);Violation of Art. 14+3 (failure to investigate possible racist motives);Pecuniary damage - claim dismissed;Non-pecuniary damage - financial award
summary:
In the case of Bekos and Koutropoulos v. Greece, the applicants, Mr. Bekos and Mr. Koutroupoulos, are Greek nationals of Roma origin living in Mesolonghi, Western Greece. Their case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma and Travellers to police violence and the failure of authorities to investigate possible racist motives behind such abuse. On 8 May 1998, following an attempted burglary, the two young men were arrested by police officers. Both applicants alleged that, during and after their arrest, they were subjected to repeated beatings, threats, and degrading treatment at the police station, including racist insults and threats of sexual violence. Medical evidence confirmed that they had suffered significant injuries consistent with their accounts.

The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Article 3 (prohibition of torture and inhuman or degrading treatment) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination) in conjunction with Article 3. The Court found that both applicants had been subjected to inhuman and degrading treatment by the police, in violation of Article 3, and that the authorities had failed to investigate whether racist motives played a role, violating Article 14 taken with Article 3. However, the Court did not find a separate violation of Article 14 and Article 3 regarding the alleged racist treatment itself. The applicants were awarded compensation for non-pecuniary damage.

This judgment is significant as it underscores the persistent problem of police violence and impunity affecting Roma and Travellers in Europe, and it reinforces the obligation of states to investigate possible racist motives in cases of ill-treatment, reflecting ongoing concerns about systemic discrimination against Roma communities.
